Abdul Quayum, Senior Advocate with Md Ali Reza, Advocate ------ For the Petitioner. 
Md Afzal Hossain, Advocate with ASM Khasru Advocate ------ For the Opposite Parties.
parties:
Maksuda Haque ------ Petitioner
Vs.
Firoz Ahmed Sharif and others ------ Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
This rule was issued calling upon the opposite party No. 1 to 3 to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and order dated 4-5-2010 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 1st Court Barisal, in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 10 of 2008 reversing those of dated 27-3-2008 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 1st Court Barisal in Miscellaneous Case No. 47 of 2005 dismissing the case should not be set aside and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem it and proper.

2. The short facts leading to the disposal of the rule is that the opposite party Nos. 1-3 as pre-emptor filed Miscellaneous Case No. 47 of 2005 in the court of learned Joint District. Judge, 1st Court, Barisal claiming pre-emption against document dated 11-5-1999 under section 24 of the Non-Agriculture Tenancy Act and the case was filed on 6-6-2005.

3. The case was filed on the allegation that the property in dispute originally belonged to Abdul Gani, who died leaving behind two sons named Kanchan Ali and Kashem Ali. Kanchan Ali died leaving behind 4 sons 3 daughters and one widow. The pre-emptors are 3 sons of Kanchan Ali and they have been in possession in their ancestral property of disputed SA khatian No. 580. The pre-emptors at first came to learn about kabala on 29-5-2005 from Alo Miah in presence of Kamrul and Somir that their uncle Kashem Ali sold 0.38 acre of land out of 0.60 acre to stranger opposite party No. 1 and got definite knowledge on 05-6-2005 after obtaining certified copy of the impugned document dated 11-5-1999. Pre-emptors had no knowledge of sale because no notice was served. The disputed land is necessary because it is adjacent to their homestead and they are co-sharers by inheritance. The disputed land is within the Barisal City Corporation hence the case was filed under section 24 of the Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act.

4. The petitioner as opposite party No. 1 appeared and contested the case by filing written objection contending inter alia that Kashem Ali sold 0.38 acre of land to this petitioner by kabala dated 11-5-1999 and delivered possession. The pre-emptors had earlier knowledge and opposite party No. 1 purchased the land when the pre-emptors refused to purchase the same due to financial inability. Opposite party No. 1 mutated Khatian No. 4409 on 9-4-2004 and has been in possession upon payment of rent and also opened separate holding in the corporation. The land under pre-emption was low and it was filed up with earth and erected structure and let out 15 cubit tin-shed room with latrine and planted many valuable trees within the knowledge of the pre-emptors. The disputed land was acquired in LA Case No. 1 of 2004-2005 for the purpose of Dapdapia Bridge and opposite party No. 1 applied for compensation. The brother of the pre-emptors named Bazlur Rahman also sold his share on 30-4-2002 to some local persons but no pre-emption was filed against this document because the consideration is higher than the earlier disputed document dated 11-5-2009 and it was disputed document dated 11-5-2009 and it was further stated that the price of the land has increased noticeably and the pre-emptors being extremely greedy are out to get this valuable land at a low price and has filed this case with false story of knowledge which is liable to be dismissed; it was alleged that price of land increased abnormally by lapse of time. Immediately after sale there was chance of possession and change of nature and character within the knowledge of the pre-emptor opposite party.

5. The case of the petitioner is that they had no knowledge of the sale by their uncle and the land is necessary because it is adjacent to their homestead and the case of opposite party No. 1 is that she has improved the land situated adjacent to the pre-emptors; homestead within their knowledge and also opened corporation holding and the instant case was filed after about 7 years.

6. Trial Judge framed as many as 6 issues as to maintainability, limitation, defect of party, whether pre-emptors are co-sharer, whether opposite party made any improvement in the case land and whether the pre-emptors are entitled to relief sought for.

7. During the course of trial pre-emptors examined 3 witnesses and opposite party No. 1 also examined 3 witnesses and adduced documentary evidence in her support.

8. Trial judge upon perusal of the pleading and hearing the parties and considering both oral and documentary evidence dismissed the case by judgment and order dated 27-3-2008 on the finding that the date of knowledge was not proved in evidence and no pre-emption was filed against other more valuable transfer.

9. The pre-emptors preferred Miscellaneous Appeal No. 10 of 2008 before the learned District Judge, Barisal which on transfer was heard by the learned Additional District Judge, 1st court, Barisal who was pleased to allow the appeal by judgment and order dated 4-5-2010.

10. Mr Abdul Quayum, the learned Senior Advocate appearing with Mr Md Ali Reza while Mr Md Afzal Hossain, the learned Advocate appearing with Mr ASM Khasru on behalf of the opposite party to oppose the rule.

11. Mr Abdul Quayum, the learned Senior Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner submits that the learned appellate court commit-ted error of law occasioning failure of justice in reversing the judgment of the learned trial court without complying with the provisions of Order 41 Rule 31 of the Code of Civil Procedure and the same being not a proper judgment of reversal is liable to be set aside.

12. He next submits that the learned appellate court upon misreading and non-consideration of material evidence failed to notice that the case land is next to homestead of the pre-emptor and opposite party has been in possession upon payment of rent Exhibit-Ga series according to Mutation Khatian Exhibit-ka and OPW-2 and OPW-3 are close neighbors of both the parties which was not denied at all by the pre-emptors and possession of opposite party for more than 6 years falsified the claim of knowledge thus the learned appellate court committed error of law occasioning failure of justice.

13. He further submits that the learned appellate court misread the evidence and wrongly found opposite party has not filed any document supporting mutation but Exhibit-ka itself is the mutation khatian and such misreading affecting the merit of the case shows that the learned court failed to apply judicial mind occasioning failure of justice.

14. Learned Advocate also submits that the learned appellate court upon misconception of law failed to appreciate that by lapse of time the claim of pre-emption has become barred by time and the learned appellate court did not assign any reason why the statement of PW 2 and PW 3 regarding knowledge could be believed and upon misreading of evidence failed to consider that pre-emptors definitely failed to discharge the heavy onus to prove knowledge thus committed error of law occasioning failure of justice.

15. He next submits that the learned appellate court did mat consider that PW 2 clearly admitted in evidence that the relation between pre-emptors and vendor-uncle was good till death of uncle and this statement makes alleged knowledge false and PW 2 also stated that he got the knowledge of the disputed purchase through one Azahar in front of Daroga Bari but this was not the case of pre-emptor and the learned appellate court committed error of law occasioning failure of justice.

16. He further submits that the pre-emption case is not maintainable because the compensation in the Land Acquisition Case which is admitted in evidence was withdrawn by petitioner thus the learned court below committed error of law occasioning failure of justice.

17. He also submits that the learned appellate court committed error of law occasioning failure of justice in reversing the judgment of the learned trial court without complying with the provisions of Order 41 Rule 31 of the Code of Civil Procedure and the same being not a proper judgment of reversal is liable to be set aside.

18. He lastly submits that the learned appellate court did not consider that PW 2 clearly admitted in evidence that the relation between pre-emptors and vendor uncle was good till death of uncle and 'this statement makes alleged knowledge and PW 2 also stated that he got the knowledge of the disputed purchase from one Azahar in front of Daroga Bari but this was not the case of pre-emptor in the application and the learned appellate court committed error of law occasioning failure of justice.

19. The learned Advocate also submits that the P.W. I made out true story about his knowledge in course as it stated filed instant case after being knowledge of the disputed document when he himself went to be withdrawal the compensation money of the statement of PW 1 the case of date of knowledge false true but the learned appellate court only reproduce the piece mill evidence of the parties. And erroneous he held that the, date of knowledge4 is proved in evidence without assigning any cogent reasons. Because he only reproduces the evidence but did not assign any reason to show that the date of knowledged is proved. In this connection the learned Counsel has referred the case of Abdul, Mazid Howlader and others vs Lahajuddin Howlader and others reported in 4 BLT (AD) 275.

20. Learned Advocate also submits that there is no enmity between the transfer of the disputed document and the pre-emptor and the compensation was admittedly given was pre-emptee considering his present possession. In this connection the learned advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner has referred the case of Mohammad Akbar Chowdhury vs Khalilur Rahman reported in 18 BLT (AD) 314. He has referred the case of Satya Ranjan vs Surendra Nath reported in 13 DLR 338.

21. Learned Advocate also submits that the judgment of the appellate court has been passed in violation of the provisions of law as contain in Order 41 Rule 31 of the Code of Civil Procedure and also the settled principle of law as decided in the case Reliable Jute Traders and another vs Sonali Bank and others reported in 7 BLC High Court Division page 16. The learned Advocate has drawn my attention to the fact that from the cross of PW I it clearly proved that it is a got up story the date of knowledge is concocted and the appellate court did not at all consider this material evidence and this non consideration of material evidence affecting the merit of the case and touching the root of the case which has occasioning failure of justice.

22. Learned Advocate for the petitioner in support of his contention has referred the case of Habibur Rahman (Md) and others vs Gulman Begum reported in 64 DLR (AD) page 133 para 17.

23. Learned Advocate lastly submits that the claim of pre-emption is a predatory right that is while the legislature has imposed condition for claiming pre-emption.

24. As against this Mr Md Afzal Hossain, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite party submits that no independent finding as to the issues framed by the trial judge and also no discussion of evidence adduced by the parties in the judgment of the trial judge. The judgment of the last court of fact is based on legal evidence.

25. Mr Afzal, has also pointed out that the trial judge is silent about his finding believe and disbelieve it is point for consideration of each case is to be decided in its own fact, circumstances and materials on record.

26. Mr Afzal also submits that the question of source of knowledge of the witnesses* is not relevant.

27. He further submits that in the instant case. OPW 1 is the constituted Attorney of the petitioner she resides in America. If any improvement is made that is done at their risk. He also submits that there is no mention about the cost incurred towards development they done it at their own risk. This also no description of the quantum of land of the khatian and also no proof as regard withdrawal of the compensation money and also did not mention any date of withdrawal of the money. So the impugned judgment of the last court of fact does not suffer from any legal infirmity material irregularity and illegality for which the appellate court judgment can be interfered with in support of his contention he has referred the case of Anowara Khatun vs Md Abdul Hye and others reported in 5 BLC (AD) 14.

28. I have heard the learned Advocate for both sides perused the impugned judgment and order of the last court of fact and also considered the submissions as advanced by the learned Advocates of both sides in support of their respective cases and also considered the citation as referred by both the learned Advocates in support of their respective contention.

29. On perusal of the impugned judgment and order of the last court of fact I find the impugned judgment and order of the last court of fact was not a proper judgment of reversal based on proper appreciation of both oral and documentary evidence on record and also in utter

violation of the settled principle of law as decided, in the case of Abdul Mazid Howlader and another vs Lahajuddin Howlader, reported in 4 BLT (AD) page 275 where our Apex Court held that:-

"In this case admittedly the application for pre-emption was filed after 7 years of transfer and a heavy burden lies on the pre-emptor to discharge the onus of proof that he filed the case within four months from the date of his knowledge. The pre-emptor having failed to discharge the initial onus by adducing cogent and reliable evidence the learned single judge ought to have held that the application for pre-emption is barred by limitation."

30. In another case of Md Akbar Chowdhury vs Khalilur Rahman reported in 18. BLT (AD) page 314 where our Apex Court held that:-

"Pre-emption petition was barred by limitation. It appears that the definite case of the pre-emptor is that he came to know about the transfer on 10-1-1997. The transfer in question is by sale deed dated 29-2-1992. Therefore after about five years the pre-emptor petitioners came to the court with the plea that they came to know about the sale on 10-1-1997 but in the petition there is no statement as when the purchaser demanded possession and whether anybody else was present at the time of such demand. The name of PW 2 was not mentioned in the pre-emption petition. Therefore the appellate court rightly disbelieved the story of knowledge of the petitioners from 10.01.1997 and the High Court Division affirmed the same.

Now let us see in rule 2 of order 6 of the Code of Civil Procedure provides that "Every pleading shall contain, and contain only, a statement in a concise form of the material facts on which the party pleading relies for his claim or defence, as the case may be, but not the evidence by which they are to be proved, and shall, when necessary, be divided into paragraphs, numbered consecutively, Dates, sums and numbers shall be expressed in figures".

31. In the case of Satya Ranjan Haldar and others vs Surendra Nath Das reported in 13 DLR 338 where it is held that:-"As to the point of limitation, on the face of the application for pre-emption, it is not of time, that is beyond four months from the date of the transfer. In order to bring his application within four months from the date of knowledge the petitioner respondent alleged that he was not aware of the transfer till he was informed by some persons mentioned in his petition. To counteract the evidence of those gentleman the purchasers asserted that soon after the purchase in the month of Falgun they went to cultivate the land. It was cultivating season. It is admitted that the petitioner respondent is holder of the land contiguous to the land transferred. There is no reason why he should not know about the fact of cultivation of the disputed land by the purchasers. The learned Sub-ordinate Judge is of the opinion that until and unless the registered kabala is taken back from the Registration office it is not possible for them to go to the land to cultivate it which is contrary to what generally happens. Generally after payment of the full consideration and execution of the kabala (where it is stated that the land has been given in possession of the transferees) the transferees take possession of the land and they never wait for getting back the registered kabala from the Registration office. In the kabala it is definitely stated: "From today you being the rightful owner of the property sold to you being fully armed with all our right, title and interest by right of purchase from us, do must happily own, possess and enjoy for time to come mutating your names in place of ours in the sherista of landlord."

32. This reasoning of the learned Sub-ordinate Judge is apparently faulty and he should not have relied on the evidence of P.W. 2 who happens to be the purohit (family Brahmin) of the petitioner respondent and admittedly who is interested in the case of the petitioner respondent.

<u>33. I find on perusal of the impugned judgment and order of the Appellate Court, the Appellate Court on total non-application and non-consideration of both oral and documentary evidence passed the impugned judgment which is based on legal perversity, material irregularity and illegality as well as such I am of the definite view that the appellate court as final court of fact can himself reassess the oral and documentary evidence under its appellate jurisdiction and both the parties are at liberty to adduce further evidence if any in support of their respective cases and the learned Appellate Court on perusal of the oral and documentary evidence and after due consideration of the same write out a fresh judgment and in that view of the matter the Miscellaneous Appeal No. 10 of 2008 is send back on remand to the appellate court for rehearing the appeal on merit and the learned Appellate Court is hereby directed to dispose of the Appeal expeditiously preferably within three months positively from the date of receipt of the copy of the judgment with this observation the rule is made absolute. The impugned judgment and order dated 4-5-2010 passed by the learned Additional District Judge 1st Court Barisal is hereby set aside.</u>

34. The order of stay as granted at the time of issuance of the rule is hereby recalled and vacated.

Send down the lower courts record along with a copy of this judgment to the concern court forthwith for information and necessary action.

End.
